🎯 Picture Quiz — Build Your Own Quiz Game!

⏱ 60 minutes 👦 Ages 9–13 🧩 ~29 blocks 💡 7 concepts

🎯 What You'll Build

You'll build your very own picture quiz game for the M5Stack Tab5! The game shows you a picture and asks you to pick the right answer from four choices. After 8 rounds, you'll see your final score — and the game remembers your best score forever, even if you turn the device off. Can you beat your own high score?

🧠 What You'll Learn

  • Variables — Named boxes where your program stores numbers, like score and current_round
  • Lists — Numbered shelves that hold lots of related things in order. Lists can even contain other lists — like a bookshelf where each shelf holds more books!
  • Event Handling — Code that waits for something to happen (like a button tap) and then springs into action
  • Conditional Logic (if/else) — Your program makes decisions: "If the answer is right, add a point!"
  • Functions — Reusable recipes you write once and call whenever you need
  • Page Navigation — Moving between different screens on your Tab5
  • NVS (Persistent Storage) — Special memory that survives turning the power off — like carving your score into stone!

📦 What You Need

  • ✅ M5Stack Tab5 controller
  • ✅ USB cable to connect to your computer
  • ✅ Flash storage with 8 quiz images pre-loaded (see Image Preparation below)
  • ✅ No extra hardware needed!
🖼️ Image Preparation — Do This Before the Lesson! Before you start coding, you need 8 pictures uploaded to your device. Save them as .jpg files on the flash storage.
  1. Find 8 images you want to quiz people about (landmarks, animals, people, planets — anything!)
  2. Resize them to about 256×256 pixels
  3. Upload them to your device at /flash/res/img/
  4. Name them Q1.jpg, Q2.jpg, Q3.jpg, Q4.jpg, Q5.jpg, Q6.jpg, Q7.jpg, Q8.jpg

🗺️ How the Program Works

Your quiz game has three screens, just like three pages in a book:

┌──────────────────────┐ │ 🎬 Title Screen │ │ Picture Quiz + START│ └────────┬─────────────┘ │ Tap START ▼ ┌──────────────────────┐ │ 🎮 Game Screen │ │ Image + 4 Buttons │ │ Round X/8 · Score:X │ └────────┬─────────────┘ │ Tap answer ▼ ┌─────────┐ │ Right? │──Yes──▶ Score +1 │ Wrong? │──No───▶ Score unchanged └────┬────┘ │ More rounds?──Yes──▶ Next round │ No ▼ ┌──────────────────────┐ │ 🏆 Game Over Screen │ │ Your Score · Best │ │ Try Again │ └──────────────────────┘ │ Tap Try Again └──▶ Back to Title Screen
🧩 What's a flowchart? It's a map of your program. Follow the arrows to see where the program goes next — just like following a treasure map!

Create Your Project and Design Three Screens

Set up your project and use the UI Editor to build all three pages

What we're doing: Every program needs a home. We'll create a new project, tell UIFlow2 we're using a Tab5, and build all three screens in the UI Editor — the title screen, the game screen, and the game-over screen.

🧩 Analogy The UI Editor is like decorating three pages of a scrapbook. You drag stickers (widgets) onto each page and position them exactly where you want. The computer remembers the layout so you don't have to describe every pixel in code.

A) Create the Project

  1. Go to uiflow2.m5stack.com
  2. Click File → New Project and name it "Picture Quiz"
  3. In the right sidebar, set Controller to Tab5 and Connection to USB
📸 Screenshot: UIFlow2 project settings

B) Open the UI Editor

  1. Click the UI Editor button in the bottom toolbar — it opens full-screen

C) Build Page 0 — The Title Screen

  1. Click page0's background in the Properties panel and set it to 0x1A237E (dark blue)
  2. Drag a Label onto the canvas. Set text to Picture Quiz, font to lv.font_montserrat_48, text color to 0xFFFFFF (white), background opacity to 0, position x=200 y=80
  3. Drag another Label. Set text to Test your knowledge!, font lv.font_montserrat_18, color 0xB0BEC5, background opacity 0, x=280 y=170
  4. Drag a Button. Set text to START, width 200 height 60, color 0x4CAF50 (green), font lv.font_montserrat_24, x=300 y=300
  5. In the component list (left panel), rename widget2 to start_btn and rename page0 to title_page
📸 Screenshot: Title screen in the UI Editor

D) Build Page 1 — The Game Screen

  1. Click the ▶ right arrow in the page bar to add a new page. Rename it to game_page and set its background to 0xECEFF1 (light gray)
  2. Drag an Image widget. Set source to Q1.jpg, position x=30 y=112. Rename it to quiz_image
  3. Drag a Label. Set text Round 1/8, font lv.font_montserrat_18, color 0x37474F, background opacity 0, x=600 y=200. Rename to round_label
  4. Drag a Label. Set text Score: 0, font lv.font_montserrat_18, color 0x37474F, background opacity 0, x=1100 y=200. Rename to score_label

Now add four answer buttons in a 2×2 grid on the right side:

  1. answer_btn1: text Answer 1, w210 h55, color 0x2196F3, font lv.font_montserrat_16, x=400 y=150
  2. answer_btn2: text Answer 2, w210 h55, color 0x2196F3, font lv.font_montserrat_16, x=800 y=150
  3. answer_btn3: text Answer 3, w210 h55, color 0x2196F3, font lv.font_montserrat_16, x=400 y=300
  4. answer_btn4: text Answer 4, w210 h55, color 0x2196F3, font lv.font_montserrat_16, x=800 y=300
📸 Screenshot: Game screen in the UI Editor

E) Build Page 2 — The Game Over Screen

  1. Click ▶ to add page2. Rename to gameover_page, background 0x1A237E
  2. Drag a Label: text Game Over!, font lv.font_montserrat_48, color 0xFFEB3B (yellow), background opacity 0, x=460 y=60
  3. Drag a Label: text Your Score: 0/8, font lv.font_montserrat_24, color 0xFFFFFF, background opacity 0, x=520 y=240. Rename to final_score_label
  4. Drag a Label: text Best Score: 0/8, font lv.font_montserrat_24, color 0xB0BEC5, background opacity 0, x=520 y=380. Rename to best_score_label
  5. Drag a Button: text Try Again, w200 h60, color 0xFF9800 (orange), font lv.font_montserrat_24, x=540 y=560. Rename to try_again_btn
  6. Close the UI Editor — your widgets appear as blocks in the workspace!
📸 Screenshot: Game Over screen in the UI Editor
✅ What you should see: Your workspace should now show: M5.begin, Widgets.setRotation, m5ui.init, three M5Page() blocks full of widgets, and a title_page screen_load block in Setup. The Loop section has M5.update.
💾 Save your progress! Great job — you've built three beautiful screens. Now let's give your game a brain!
